name: Brute Force
description: Adversaries guess passwords repeatedly, e.g. many failed logins (EventID 4625, SSH failures) from one source.

name: Command and Scripting Interpreter: PowerShell
description: Abuse of PowerShell to run commands, encoded commands (-enc), download cradles such as IEX DownloadString, often spawned by Office apps.

name: Phishing: Spearphishing Attachment
description: Malicious email attachments such as macro-enabled documents (.docm) delivered to users.

name: Valid Accounts
description: Use of legitimate credentials, e.g. impossible travel or logins from unusual locations.

name: Remote Services: Remote Desktop Protocol
description: Logging in to hosts via RDP, especially first-seen sources or off-hours sessions.

name: Data Encrypted for Impact
description: Ransomware: mass file encryption or renaming, ransom notes, rapid file modification.

name: OS Credential Dumping: LSASS Memory
description: Reading lsass.exe memory to extract credentials, e.g. procdump or mimikatz.

name: Network Service Discovery
description: Port scanning or service enumeration across hosts or subnets.

name: Application Layer Protocol: Web Protocols
description: C2 over HTTP/HTTPS, including periodic beaconing with regular intervals and similar payload sizes.

name: Exfiltration Over Alternative Protocol
description: Large transfers of data over FTP, DNS or other non-standard channels to external servers.

name: Exploit Public-Facing Application
description: Exploitation of internet-facing services, e.g. Log4Shell JNDI strings, SMB exploits, web app vulnerabilities.

name: Scheduled Task/Job: Scheduled Task
description: Creation of scheduled tasks to run malicious code or maintain persistence.

name: Indicator Removal: Clear Windows Event Logs
description: Clearing Windows event logs (EventID 1102 security log cleared) to hide activity.

name: Impair Defenses: Disable or Modify Tools
description: Disabling security tooling such as Windows Defender real-time protection or EDR agents.

name: Boot or Logon Autostart: Registry Run Keys
description: Adding Run/RunOnce registry keys so a program starts at logon.
